text:
infra-bot: ALERT: spike in 429s for /v1/generate across multiple regions (us-east1, eu-west1). 5xxs stable, quota backend returning DENIED for many keys. alert_id=QRP-17825
alex: I'm seeing the same in traces — looks like per-key limits are being applied at org scope. :eyes:
morgan: dashboard shows a sudden jump at 12:14 UTC, correlates with a console config change by `devon` 12:12 UTC. link: https://console.redwood.dev/rate-limits/changes
devon: that was me — I pushed a change to the default quota propagation code to make per-org defaults easier to manage. I tested locally but maybe the rollout hit prod too broadly. rolling back now.
priya: can you pause the rollout? apps are hitting 429s mid-flight, customers reporting degraded UX.
devon: issuing rollback patch to config-service: `PATCH /api/v1/configs/quotas/default` payload: ```json {"propagate_to":"org"} ``` rolling to canary then prod.
alex: quick note: the bug seems to normalize API keys to org IDs at the cache layer, so when propagate_to changed it wrote org entries for all keys in cache, effectively applying org quotas to per-key tokens.
daniel: yeah I can confirm cache writes show org:{org_id}:quota set for many token ids. looks like a missing namespacing prefix in commit 5f9b2c.
morgan: mitigation idea: flip cache read fallback to per-key first, then org, so even if writes wrong, reads prefer original key entry. low-risk toggle. thoughts?
devon: that patch is safe to flip now. applying toggle in config-service: `ENABLE_KEY_FIRST_READ=true`.
deploy-bot: deploy started: config-service v2.14.7 -> rolling to prod (canary 1/3) by devon. 1782504450
priya: notify support and PGs to expect reduced 429s in ~2m after canary.
alex: after canary succeeded, we should run a backfill to remove org-scoped entries created by bad write. I'll script it but holding until rates normalize.
daniel: digging into logs: offending writes started at 12:12:04 UTC and stopped at 12:13:10 UTC — estimate ~120k cache keys affected. backfill needs to scan and delete org-scoped keys with write_ts in that window.
morgan: alerting SRE runbook: #oncall_quota_mispropagation. @oncall page.
infra-bot: METRIC: 429_rate /v1/generate peaked at 18% of requests at 12:15, down to 6% after canary toggle.
devon: canary looked clean, rolling rest of fleet.
deploy-bot: deploy success: config-service v2.14.7 -> prod complete. 1782504560
priya: I'm seeing customer reports drop off. good. please post postmortem with timeline and owners.
alex: noted — will create incident postmortem and include mitigations: change gating for console quota rollout, add a preflight that simulates cache writes, and add automated rollback if 429s > 5% in 5m window.
daniel: also adding a readonly mode for the cache when propagation mode changes to prevent mass writes.
morgan: thanks everyone. closing alert but keeping thread open until postmortem published. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident resolved: QRP-17825 resolved at 12:31 UTC.
